summary: SoftBank Corp is investing €473 million ($513M) for a 51% stake in Dublin-based Cubic Telecom, which provides software-based connectivity for vehicles across mobile networks worldwide, valuing it at just over $1 billion. The deal makes Cubic a consolidated SoftBank subsidiary and supports SoftBank's 'Beyond Japan' strategy for expanding into IoT connectivity. Cubic acts as a wholesale aggregator so automakers avoid region-by-region carrier deals, and it is growing fast as connected-car adoption rises.
one_line: SoftBank Corp pays $513M for 51% of Dublin-based Cubic Telecom, a connected-car connectivity provider valued at just over $1 billion.
key_facts: SoftBank Corp is investing €473 million ($513 million) in Cubic Telecom for a 51% stake.
The deal values Dublin-based Cubic Telecom at just over $1 billion (€927 million) and makes it a consolidated subsidiary of SoftBank.
Barry Napier stays on as Cubic Telecom CEO and keeps a board seat; SoftBank SVP of global business Daichi Nozaki and two other SoftBank appointees join the board.
The remaining three board seats go to existing investors, including CARIAD (Volkswagen Group) and Qualcomm.
Cubic Telecom has partnerships with 90 national and multinational mobile network operators and connects 17 million+ vehicles in 190 countries and regions.
Cubic Telecom COO Shane Sorohan said this is only 7% to 10% of the market; Juniper Research estimates around 192 million connected vehicles today.
Cubic Telecom connects about 450,000 new vehicles each month, and orders are expected to raise that rate 'exponentially' over five years.
McKinsey forecasts 95% of new vehicles will be sold with built-in wireless connectivity by 2030; Juniper projects just under 400 million connected new cars by then.
The investment comes from SoftBank Corp., the Japanese telecoms and IT division in Tokyo, not SoftBank Group or the Vision Fund.
Cubic Telecom has already been integrating SoftBank's wireless network in Japan to connect cars.
Cubic Telecom appeared at TechCrunch's first-ever Battlefield in 2007, when it focused on helping consumers connect phones while roaming.
Cubic acts as a wholesale aggregator, sparing automakers from cutting deals with individual carriers region-by-region.
Cubic could also serve other verticals such as agriculture, per Sorohan.
SoftBank Corp. CEO Junichi Miyakawa tied the deal to the 'Beyond Japan' strategic growth initiative.
